inputs.userGoal: Implement private networking (VNet-integrated Container Apps environment, Azure Files private endpoint and private DNS)
subGoals: Preserve existing data and enforced storage security policy
Use additive migration with explicit new URLs and no resource deletion
Keep SQLite single-writer access across both old and new apps
insightsApplied: storage: connect privately rather than weakening network policy
registry, identity, logs: reference existing platform resources
legacy-environment, legacy-api, legacy-frontend: retain during migration

reasoning.whyChosen: Provide isolated subnets for Consumption workload profiles and private storage connectivity
reasoning.tradeoffs: Additional managed network resources and associated charges

reasoning.whyChosen: Route SMB to the existing storage account over a private IP
alternativesConsidered: ephemeral SQLite, rejected because data would be lost
reasoning.tradeoffs: Private endpoint hourly and data-processing charges

properties.existingStorageMountAuthentication: account key, retrieved at deployment and never output

reasoning.whyChosen: The existing environment has no VNet integration; new apps avoid replacing it
alternativesConsidered: delete and recreate the original environment, rejected as destructive
reasoning.tradeoffs: New app URLs, inherited SMB key mount retained; managed-identity SMB is a separate preview migration requiring storage settings changes

overallReasoning.summary: Add private connectivity and replacement apps while retaining existing platform resources and data.
overallReasoning.tradeoffs: New URLs and networking charges; no HA or premium compute for this lab. Existing ACR access and key-based SMB authentication are unchanged. Existing API revisions must stop before replacement writes to SQLite. No resources are deleted.

plan.validation: Compile both entrypoints, preview additive changes with what-if, validate workflow shell and bounded product JSON smoke test. Deployment requires separate approval.
